results.question: What is the searchable data retention period?
results.answer:
Based on the authoritative company documentation:

• Effective 2026-01-15, raw run records are held in cold recovery storage for 20 days after their plan-specific searchable retention period ends, then permanently deleted. This policy supersedes the earlier 60-day cold-storage period. (Source: Data retention policy, [retention:0])
• Deleted-account data is purged within 10 days. Backups are retained for 28 days. Cold recovery storage is not normally searchable through AQL, so it must not be added to the advertised searchable retention window. (Source: Data retention policy, [retention:1])
• Queries read the hot store for the most recent 5 days and object storage for older data. Results are cached for 8 minutes. An explicit bypass_cache option is available to workspace admins; it does not increase query limits or retention. (Source: AQL query reference, [query:2])
• Explorer timeline retention is 14 days on Team and 60 days on Enterprise. This is separate from searchable run-record retention. Sampling is 50% on Team and 100% on Enterprise, selected deterministically by run_id. (Source: Run Explorer specification, [traces:1])
• Duplicate submissions with the same event_id are suppressed for 48 hours. Records older than 96 hours are accepted with late=true. Each record supports at most 80 custom attributes and each attribute value is limited to 2 KB. results.question: What data is retained and for how long at each stage of the retention lifecycle?
results.answer:
Based on the authoritative company documentation:

• Deleted-account data is purged within 10 days. Backups are retained for 28 days. Cold recovery storage is not normally searchable through AQL, so it must not be added to the advertised searchable retention window. (Source: Data retention policy, [retention:1])
• Queries read the hot store for the most recent 5 days and object storage for older data. Results are cached for 8 minutes. An explicit bypass_cache option is available to workspace admins; it does not increase query limits or retention. (Source: AQL query reference, [query:2])
• Writers store recent data in ClickHouse and longer-lived records as Parquet in object storage. The hot-store window is 5 days. The Heron query engine routes reads based on the requested time range and merges results when a query crosses that boundary. (Source: Ingestion and query architecture, [architecture:1])
• Production deployments use blue/green releases with canary stages at 10%, 40%, and 100%. Each stage has a 15-minute observation period. Operators record the release version and deployment identifier before starting. (Source: Deployment runbook, [deploy:0])
• Check searchable record retention and Run Explorer retention separately. For a region move, create a new project and redirect future ingestion; historical records are not migrated automatically. The current pricing and region documents govern eligibility. (Source: Customer onboarding guide, [onboarding:2])

results.question: What changed between Asterline v2.0 and v2.1 in terms of ingestion limits and warehouse support?
results.answer:
Based on the authoritative company documentation:

• Version 2.1 shipped on 2025-11-18. It introduced EU projects in Dublin for Team and Enterprise and seasonal anomaly alerting. Launch ingestion increased from 180 to 300 requests per second per project. Other plan ingestion limits stayed unchanged. (Source: Version 2.1 release notes, [release-21:0])
• Per-workspace query concurrency is 6 on Launch, 30 on Team, and 120 on Enterprise. Queries beyond this limit are rejected with 429. Ingestion limits are per project and must not be confused with these workspace query limits. (Source: AQL query reference, [query:1])
• Version 2.0 shipped on 2025-08-12. It introduced the Queuefin ingestion pipeline and Run Explorer for Team and Enterprise. Launch ingestion was limited to 180 requests per second per project at this release. (Source: Version 2.0 release notes, [release-20:0])
• The per-project ingestion rate limit is 300 requests per second on Launch, 1500 on Team, and 6000 on Enterprise. A rate-limited request returns 429 and a Retry-After header. Clients should honor the header, use bounded retries, and retain stable event identifiers when retrying. (Source: Run ingestion API, [ingest:1])
• Launch allows 6 alert rules per project, Team 75, and Enterprise 600. Warehouse Export is unavailable on Launch and included on Team and Enterprise. SAML SSO is Enterprise only. Team and Enterprise can create EU projects. Launch supports US projects only. A trial lasts 10 days with Team features and (Source: Plans and billing, [pricing:2])

• Effective 2026-01-15, raw run records are held in cold recovery storage for 20 days after their plan-specific searchable retention period ends, then permanently deleted. This policy supersedes the earlier 60-day cold-storage period. (Source: Data retention policy, [retention:0])

results.answer:

Based on the authoritative company documentation:

• Signals evaluate workflow metrics every 4 minutes. Supported modes are static threshold, percentage change against a previous period, and seasonal anomaly. Seasonal anomaly requires 21 complete days of history. Rules with insufficient history remain in a warming-up state. (Source: Signals alert rules, [alerts:0])
• Supported destinations are email, Slack, webhook, and PagerDuty. PagerDuty was added in version 2.3. Limits are 6 rules per project on Launch, 75 on Team, and 600 on Enterprise. A muted rule still evaluates but does not deliver notifications. (Source: Signals alert rules, [alerts:1])
• Asterline Labs is a fictional workflow-monitoring software company. Its product, Asterline, collects workflow runs, helps teams investigate failures, and sends operational alerts. • Asterline is a workflow-monitoring service. Run Explorer displays workflow attempts and status changes; it does not capture screens or DOM content. Signals notifications can be delayed during incidents even when the underlying run records remain available. (Source: Product FAQ, [faq:0])
• Asterline has a US region in Virginia and an EU region in Dublin. US is the default. EU projects are available on Team and Enterprise starting with version 2.1. Launch workspaces can create only US projects. (Source: Regions and workspace setup, [regions:0])
